pr.title: libjpeg-turbo: use the clz intrinsic and enable the x86_64 SIMD kernels
pr.body:
### Problem
- x64 builds compiled libjpeg-turbo with no SIMD at all (`simd = cfg.arm64` in `scripts/build/deps/libjpeg-turbo.ts`). The upstream x86_64 kernels are NASM syntax and were never wired into the direct build, so `Bun.Image` JPEG encode and decode ran the plain C code on x64 while arm64 had Neon.
- On x64 the C Huffman encoders count bits through a 64 KB `jpeg_nbits_table`. `src/jpeg_nbits.h` only switches to the clz intrinsic on Arm.

### Fix
- `scripts/build/deps/libjpeg-turbo.ts`: assemble the 27 `simd/x86_64/*.asm` files from upstream's `simd/CMakeLists.txt` (SSE2 and AVX2 kernels plus `jsimdcpu.asm`) through the existing `nasm` ninja rule, compile `simd/x86_64/jsimd.c`, and define `WITH_SIMD` on x64 too. The nasm flags are upstream's: `-felf64|-fmacho64|-fwin64`, `-DELF|-DMACHO|-DWIN64`, `-D__x86_64__`. `-DPIC` is not passed: no x86_64 kernel uses the PIC macros (they are i386 only) and the objects link into the PIE android build as well.
- `jsimd.c` selects AVX2, SSE2 or C per call from `jpeg_simd_cpu_support()` (CPUID leaf 7 plus XGETBV), so the AVX2 objects are safe under the `-march=nehalem` floor. `JSIMD_FORCESSE2=1` and `JSIMD_FORCENONE=1` still work as upstream.
- `-DUSE_CLZ_INTRINSIC` on non-arm64 targets makes the C encoders (`jcphuff.c` always, `jchuff.c` when SIMD is off) use `bsr`. With SIMD on, `jchuff-sse2.asm` ships its own copy of the table, so this no longer changes the binary size. The comment in the build file says so.
- `scripts/build/tools.ts` looks nasm up on every host. `compile.ts:nasm()` still fails with the install hint when it is missing. `bootstrap.sh` already installed nasm on Linux and `bootstrap.ps1` on Windows. `bootstrap.sh` now installs it on macOS too. `.buildkite/ci.mjs` runs the best-effort install for every x64 target.
- `scripts/verify-baseline-static/allowlist-x64.txt` and `allowlist-x64-windows.txt`: one group for the 38 `jsimd_*_avx2` kernels, ceiling `[AVX, AVX2]`. The ELF list has 282 names because nasm puts the local labels of each kernel into `.symtab` and the scanner attributes the hits to them. The names are the ones the linux-x64, linux-x64-musl and windows-x64 scans of build 100872 printed. `llint_op_wide16_wide16` joins the existing LLInt data-in-text group: the new code moved the decoder desync to a sibling handler.
- `test/js/bun/jsc-stress/fixtures/simd-baseline.test.ts` (the file the emulated verify-baseline step runs) now encodes and decodes a 72x40 JPEG. A flat grey image has to survive encode, decode and encode byte for byte, which checks the kernel results. A gradient goes through the baseline and progressive encoders. Under `qemu-x86_64 -cpu Nehalem` a bad gate traps here.
- Size, from the binary-size step of build 100872 against main: x64 targets grow by 120 KB (windows) to 146 KB (android), aarch64 targets are unchanged. The kernels and the table in `jchuff-sse2.asm` are that growth.

### Verification
- 120 cases (4 sizes including odd widths, 5 patterns, quality 1/75/100, baseline and progressive), each encoded and then decoded back to a stored PNG: the sha256 of every JPEG and of every decoded image is identical between the C-only release build of main, this branch with AVX2 (default on the test host), this branch with `JSIMD_FORCESSE2=1`, and this branch with `JSIMD_FORCENONE=1`.
- gdb hit counts on one 96x80 round trip: by default `jsimd_fdct_islow_avx2`, `jsimd_idct_islow_avx2` and `jsimd_quantize_avx2` run 180 times each and the h2v2 down/upsample AVX2 kernels 80 times, so the dispatch picks AVX2 and the 32-byte alignment of the constants survived the link. With `JSIMD_FORCESSE2=1` the SSE2 kernels take the same counts and no AVX2 kernel runs.
- `test/js/bun/image/*.test.ts` pass on the x64 debug build. The new simd-baseline cases pass natively, with `JSIMD_FORCESSE2=1`, with `JSIMD_FORCENONE=1`, and under `qemu-x86_64 -cpu Nehalem`.
- Build 100872 built and linked all 12 targets (elf64, macho64, win64, and the PIE android link). Its only failures were the three verify-baseline steps. With the allowlist commit (build 100910) all seven verify-baseline steps pass: the linux-x64 scan reports 0 violations and 1070 allowlisted symbols, windows-x64 0 and 876, and the stale counts did not move. The two JPEG cases ran and passed under QEMU on linux-x64 and linux-x64-musl and under Intel SDE on windows-x64.
- Configure on an x64 host now needs nasm installed, because the libjpeg-turbo `.asm` edges are emitted at configure time. The rust-lint GitHub action installs it for that reason.

### Background
- libjpeg-turbo has one C implementation of each stage (colour conversion, chroma sampling, DCT, quantization, Huffman coding) and optional SIMD versions. `jsimd.c` is the per-architecture dispatcher: the C code asks `jsimd_can_*()` once per compress or decompress object and calls `jsimd_*()` if it says yes. The SIMD versions are specified to produce the same output as the C code, which is what the byte comparisons above confirm.
- The x86_64 kernels are written for nasm, which clang cannot assemble. bun already had a `nasm` ninja rule for BoringSSL's win-x64 assembly. A `direct` dependency lists its sources, and `emitDirect` routes `.asm` entries to that rule.
- verify-baseline has two parts: a static scan of `.text` that fails on any instruction beyond Nehalem unless the containing symbol is allowlisted with a feature ceiling, and an emulated run of `simd-baseline.test.ts` on a Nehalem CPU model, where an instruction the gate should have kept out raises SIGILL.

<details>
<summary>Earlier description</summary>

The PR started as the `USE_CLZ_INTRINSIC` change alone. On its own it removed the 64 KB `jpeg_nbits_table` from every x64 build (build 100478: exactly -64 KB on each x64 target, 40 of 40 encodes byte-identical). The SIMD commit brings the table back through `jchuff-sse2.asm`, so that size win no longer applies to the combined change.

</details>
